correctness.rationale: The numerator of t_S is ka(x²+kappa y²)+a(1+kappa)xy sum_epsilon_i, where iid epsilon_i are fair row-products. Negativity is equivalent to cross-sign and |B|/k>(x²+kappa y²)/((1+kappa)|xy|). AM-GM sharply minimizes the right-hand threshold at chi=2sqrt(kappa)/(1+kappa), attained for |x/y|=sqrt(kappa), and binomial signs enumerate B=2J-k. With sketch-null direction denominator zero, numerator zero and minnorm t=0, so no negative event. For kappa=1 numerator=||Sb||². Negative t strictly raises true Euclidean residual since b^T A b>0. Independent exact sign enumeration of all row-product configurations k=1..7 and four square ratios reproduced the sharp tails and endpoints. The infinite k/real kappa theorem comes from AM-GM, not sampling.
